goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest uniqueness is only enforced client-side; server schema accepts duplicates, and duplicate check against existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`) is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendee records and duplicate calendar/email sends in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The client dialog refines the email array to ensure uniqueness, but the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` (no uniqueness). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters only against existing `booking.attendees` and a blacklist, and does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array, so duplicate inputs can be persisted/sent. Additionally, the check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive and `guest` is not normalized (while blacklist emails are lowercased), so an email differing only by case can bypass the existing-attendee check and be added again, potentially causing duplicate attendee records and duplicate downstream calendar/email effects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on `booking.status`, allowing guests to be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings and sending 'CONFIRMED' iCal REQUEST emails for unconfirmed events in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:43-49

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` loads the booking (via `prisma.booking.findFirst`) but never checks any `booking.status`/state before mutating attendees and updating external calendars (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`). It then sends emails whose ICS payloads are hard-coded with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` in both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, regardless of whether the booking is cancelled/rejected/pending. This is a verifiable correctness issue introduced by the diff: the endpoint will allow adding guests and emitting confirmed invites for non-confirmed bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EventManager` constructed with `ctx.user`'s credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so calendar attendee updates run against wrong or missing calendar credentials and fail or mutate the wrong calendar in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:160-165

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking organizer can differ from the authenticated caller (`ctx.user`): the caller may be a team admin/owner or even an attendee (`isTeamAdminOrOwner` / `isAttendee` checks). However, the code builds `EventManager` using `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and spreads `...user` (which is `ctx.user`) into the constructor, then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The diff also fetches `booking.user` including `credentials` but never uses them, and separately fetches `organizer` details. This makes it verifiable that calendar updates will be attempted with the caller’s credentials rather than the booking organizer’s, which can fail (missing creds) or update the wrong calendar when the caller is not the organizer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: For seated event types, attendees are created via raw `createMany`, bypassing seat/`bookingSeat` logic (seat counts, `seatsShowAttendees` handling), potentially overbooking seats and producing inconsistent attendee state in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:96-105

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` updates `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without any logic that considers seated/capacity settings (e.g., `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`) or any seat-allocation model. The handler also doesn’t check remaining capacity before inserting new attendees, so for seated event types it can add attendees beyond the allowed seats, leading to inconsistent state (attendees list grows while seat constraints/assignments, if any, are not enforced/updated). This is directly observable in the diff: attendees are inserted in bulk and no seat-related checks/updates occur.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound on the `guests` array, allowing any attendee to add thousands of guests in a single request, triggering mass emails and calendar updates with no rate limiting — an abuse/DoS vector in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler will (1) `createMany` attendees for all provided emails, (2) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`, and (3) call `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` to enqueue emails. Additionally, the permission check allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to invoke this mutation. With no server-side cap or throttling visible in the diff, a single request could include a very large `guests` array, causing heavy DB writes, calendar updates, and mass email sending—an abuse/DoS vector introduced/left unmitigated by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Read-then-write race condition: two concurrent `addGuests` mutations both read the attendee list, pass the duplicate check, and insert the same guests, yielding duplicate attendees and duplicate emails in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:85-105

adjudication.rationale: In addGuestsHandler, the code first reads the booking and its current attendees (findFirst include attendees), then computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already present in that snapshot, and finally writes via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. These steps are not wrapped in a transaction and there is no `skipDuplicates`/upsert-style protection shown, so two concurrent mutations can both observe the same pre-insert attendee list, both accept the same guest emails as “unique”, and both attempt to insert them. Whether this results in actual duplicate rows or a DB constraint error depends on schema constraints not shown here, but the TOCTOU race described is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Catch block does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err`, destroying diagnostic information; should log the error (or use the logger) and consider surfacing partial failure to the caller in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170-172

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code wraps sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) in a try/catch and the catch block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging the caught `err` (and without rethrowing). This is directly visible in the diff and it does discard the actual error details, making failures hard to diagnose and silently allowing email-sending failures to pass as success to the caller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isInvalidEmail` is set on failed validation but never cleared when the user edits the emails or when the dialog is reopened after successful submission, leaving a stale error banner in apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:44-52

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails in `handleAdd`, but it is only cleared in the Cancel button handler. It is not cleared when the user edits the email fields (`MultiEmail` just updates `multiEmailValue`) and it is not cleared on successful submission (`onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` but never calls `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Since the dialog component stays mounted and is only toggled via the `open` prop, reopening after a prior validation failure can show a stale error banner even with fresh/empty inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }` with `findFirstOrThrow` throws an opaque Prisma 'record not found' error for bookings with a null `userId` instead of a meaningful error in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:57

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined` (which the `|| 0` suggests is possible), this will query for user id 0 and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw Prisma's generic “record not found” error. There is no explicit check for a missing organizer userId and no TRPCError wrapping here, so the client would receive an opaque internal error instead of a meaningful domain error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message fallback `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable since `message` is always non-empty, and `t()` is applied to arbitrary server messages that aren't translation keys, showing users raw error codes in apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:57

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, `message` is built via a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. Template literals always produce a string, and this one will be non-empty in practice even when `err.data?.code` is undefined (e.g. "undefined: ...") or when `err.message` is an empty string (e.g. "BAD_REQUEST: "). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will essentially never hit the fallback, making that fallback effectively unreachable. Additionally, the code prefixes the toast with `err.data?.code` (e.g. BAD_REQUEST/FORBIDDEN), which will be shown to end users as a raw error code. The point about `t(err.message)` translating arbitrary messages is less strictly provable from this diff (the server-side messages added here are translation keys), but the unreachable fallback and raw code display are verifiable in the diff.
